attacks.title: Private initialization precedes every receiving process
attacks.claim: The three positive secrecy/authentication results describe an executing adversarial-review protocol.
attacks.observation: All receivers lie in the continuation after the first private output. Under synchronous private communication the initial output cannot rendezvous; protocol roles never run. ProVerif returns all three original queries true, but added reachability queries cannot reconstruct traces.
attacks.counterfactual: Direct private parameter provisioning makes RedWrites, LeadEmitsToDefense and DefenseLearnsRed reachable with concrete traces, while all three security queries remain true; seeded plaintext leaks then yield false with traces.
attacks.qualification: Deadlock is a source-level process-semantics argument. ProVerif says cannot be proved for reachability, not proved unreachable. This is a vacuity/model-initialization finding, not a cryptographic break.
attacks.close_with: Reachable initialization plus positive event traces and seeded confidentiality/authentication mutation controls.

attacks.title: One defense-key send cannot provision two consuming roles
attacks.target: proofs/coordination/isolation.pv def_keychan producer and two inputs
attacks.claim: Both the defense publisher and Gate-B receiver participate in one round.
attacks.observation: After parallelizing private key distribution, only one defense role can consume the sole key tuple. A joint DefenseWrites-and-DefenseLearnsRed marker has no reconstructable trace; providing a second tuple produces a concrete joint trace.
attacks.qualification: This latent modeling bug is exposed after fixing R1-RED-001. Non-reachability follows from one-send/two-consumer resource counting; ProVerif does not itself prove non-reachability here.
attacks.close_with: Provision every role explicitly, then require a single trace witnessing both defense publication and Gate-B receipt.

attacks.title: Authenticated lead emission does not enforce seal-before-delivery
attacks.target: skills/redteam-review/references/comms-protocol.md sealed round lifecycle and isolation.pv S3
attacks.claim: White receives red plaintext only after the attack manifest has been sealed.
attacks.observation: In the live-provisioning variant, insert AttackManifestSealed immediately after the red output and ask DefenseLearnsRed(red_msg) ==> AttackManifestSealed. ProVerif returns false with a concrete trace; original S1/S2/S3 still hold. The lead can relay the first ciphertext before the red continuation seals.
attacks.qualification: Counterexample applies to the instrumented, operational repaired harness and the stronger lifecycle claim. The original S3 is only source authentication; no claim of an exploit in a deployed daemon.
attacks.close_with: Model a sealed manifest identity and explicit release gate; bind delivered content to that identity; prove seal precedes release and include reachable success plus early-delivery mutant.
